claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex. It's helpful to know he's 8 years old.

Now, could you please tell me if you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. 

Do you live with Alex, or if not, do you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit (currently £25.60 per week for an eldest or only child) towards looking after him — for example, on food, clothes, or pocket money?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know.

Just a couple more questions to make sure we cover everything:

Is Alex currently living at home with you full-time, or is he in hospital, care, or any kind of residential accommodation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, he's been in hospital for a few months now. But he still lives with me normally - this is just temporary while he's getting treatment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to hear Alex is in hospital. I hope his treatment goes well.

Could you tell me roughly how long Alex has been in hospital? Specifically, has it been more than 12 weeks?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Let me think... it's been about 12 weeks, I believe. Right around that mark.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex has been in hospital for around 12 weeks, there's an important detail I need to check.

Do you regularly spend money on Alex while he's in hospital — for example, on things like clothes, toys, treats, or other items for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I still buy him clothes, magazines, and his favorite snacks and food when I visit. I make sure he has what he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great to hear that you're continuing to support Alex while he's in hospital.

Just one more question: Is anyone else currently claiming or planning to claim Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. It's just me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

- ✅ **Age**: Alex is 8 years old, which is under the age of 16
- ✅ **UK residence**: You live in the UK
- ✅ **Responsibility**: Alex normally lives with you, so you're responsible for him
- ✅ **Hospital stay exception**: Although Alex has been in hospital for around 12 weeks (the usual time limit), you continue to regularly spend money on him (clothes, magazines, snacks, food). This means you qualify for an exception that allows Child Benefit to continue for children in UK hospitals
- ✅ **No competing claims**: No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

**Important**: Since Alex has been in hospital for around 12 weeks, you should inform HMRC about his hospital stay if you haven't already. You can do this by filling in an online form or contacting HMRC directly. This will ensure your payments continue without interruption, as you meet the exception criteria.

I wish Alex a speedy recovery!

The claimant has confirmed they regularly spend money on Alex while he's in hospital (clothes, magazines, snacks, food), which satisfies this exception. No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. Therefore, the claimant is eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
